sections.content: Now p count increased to 12 after clicking empty region. So any click anywhere increments progress. So goal is to fill progress bar to full. So we need to click enough times to fill to 64 p's. Currently 12 p's. Need 52 more clicks. That's many but still manageable. However we have action budget; we can batch many MOUSE actions in one call. The harness will stop early if a no-impact action occurs (but clicks always cause board change until bar full). So we can send a batch of many clicks. We need to know when bar completes: maybe when p count reaches 64, then level completes automatically. So we can click many times at any location. Let's click at same coordinate (e.g., row 60 col 30) repeatedly 52 times in a batch. Use intent='solve' to bypass no-impact check? Actually we want to ensure they all cause change; they will until full. Use intent='solve' to avoid early stop on no-impact (but after full, further clicks might be no-impact and stop). But we can just send 52 clicks; after bar full, further clicks may be no-impact but they will stop early. That's fine. Let's compute needed clicks: target 64 p's. Current count 12. Need 52. We'll send 52 MOUSE clicks at same spot.

sections.label: TOOL CALL: python
sections.content:
<tool_call>
<function=python>
<parameter=code>
# Determine current p count
p_count = current_frame.ascii.split('\n')[-1].count('p')
need = 64 - p_count
print('need', need)
actions = []
for i in range(need):
    actions.append({'action':'MOUSE','row':60,'col':30})
# execute batch with intent solve to avoid stop on no-impact
action(actions, intent='solve')
print('after batch state', last_action_result.get('state'))
print('board_changed', last_action_result.get('board_changed'))
print('new p count', current_frame.ascii.split('\n')[-1].count('p'))
</parameter>
</function>
</tool_call>
